c.tagline: Sri Lanka's hill-country cultural capital, home to the sacred Temple of the Tooth

taxi.fareNote: Metered tuk-tuks and the PickMe app are the norm; agree on a price beforehand for unmetered rides

emergency.note: 119 reaches police emergency services; 1990 is the Suwa Seriya free ambulance line

hood_landmark.City Center/Lake: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

avoid.reason: Fake "helpful guide" touts around the Temple of the Tooth; tuk-tuk overcharging

hood_desc: The City Center around Kandy Lake is the heart of the city, home to the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, the Kandy National Museum, and the lakeside promenade lined with markets, restaurants, and colonial-era buildings.
Peradeniya, a few kilometers southwest, is known for its sprawling Royal Botanical Gardens and the university, giving the area a leafy, academic character with guesthouses catering to visitors.
Katukele climbs the hillside above the lake to the giant Bahirawakanda Buddha statue, offering panoramic views over the city and a quieter, more residential feel.
Getambe, further along the river toward Peradeniya, is a low-key residential and small-business area popular for mid-range guesthouses within easy reach of the botanical gardens.
Ampitiya is a hillside residential district east of the center with churches and schools, offering a calmer, local-life alternative to the tourist core.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not recommended.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5am-9pm; fewer trains after evening
transit.pay: Cash paid on board buses; paper tickets for trains
transit.map: No unified app; Kandy Central Bus Stand is the main hub
transit.note: Public buses and three-wheelers (tuk-tuks) are the main way to get around; the scenic railway line links Kandy to Colombo, Nuwara Eliya, and Ella

train: Scenic line to Colombo Fort (~2.5-3h) and onward to Nanu Oya/Ella through the hill country
bus: Frequent intercity and express buses connect Kandy to Colombo, Nuwara Eliya, and other cities

tip.r: Not obligatory but 10% in restaurants without a service charge, and small amounts for drivers and guides, are common and welcomed
